en.objective: Give instructions with the base verb, use Don't + base verb to stop someone, and Let's + base verb to suggest. Example: It's cold outside. Put on your jacket!
en.misconception: Learner adds a subject, -s, -ing, or to to the command, or uses 'not' alone to stop someone.
en.reasoning: identify the sentence as an instruction -> check that there is no subject -> choose the plain verb
en.stem: It's cold outside. ___ your jacket!

distractors.misconception: adding -s as if the command needed subject-verb agreement with a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: It adds -s, but a command has no subject to match.

distractors.misconception: using the -ing form on its own, which describes an activity instead of telling someone to act
distractors.whyFails: It only names an activity; it does not tell anyone to act.

distractors.misconception: using a to-infinitive where a direct command is required
distractors.whyFails: It starts with to, but a command starts with the verb itself.

explanation.whyCorrect: This is an instruction to you, so it starts with the base verb, Put on.
explanation.rule: Command: base verb (Open, Sit). Warning: Don't + base verb (Don't run). Suggestion: Let's + base verb (Let's go).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Puts on' adds -s, 'Putting on' only names an activity, and 'To put on' is not a command.
explanation.howToAvoid: Start with the verb itself: no subject, no -s, no -ing, no to.
explanation.memoryCue: Commands start with the plain verb: Put on, Sit down, Look.

id_.objective: Beri perintah dengan kata kerja bentuk dasar, pakai “Don't” + bentuk dasar untuk melarang, dan “Let's” + bentuk dasar untuk mengajak. Contoh: “It's cold outside. Put on your jacket!”
id_.misconception: Kamu menambahkan subjek, -s, -ing, atau “to” pada kalimat perintah, atau memakai “not” saja untuk melarang.
id_.reasoning: pastikan kalimatnya perintah → cek nggak ada subjeknya → pilih kata kerja bentuk dasar
id_.rule: Perintah: kata kerja bentuk dasar (“Open”, “Sit”). Larangan: “Don't” + bentuk dasar (“Don't run”). Ajakan: “Let's” + bentuk dasar (“Let's go”).
id_.whyCorrect: Ini perintah untuk kamu, jadi langsung dimulai dengan kata kerja bentuk dasar, yaitu “Put on”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Puts on” menambah -s, “Putting on” cuma menyebut kegiatan, dan “To put on” bukan kalimat perintah.
id_.howToAvoid: Mulai langsung dari kata kerjanya: tanpa subjek, tanpa -s, tanpa -ing, tanpa “to”.
id_.memoryCue: Perintah dimulai dengan kata kerja bentuk dasar: “Put on”, “Sit down”, “Look”.

Puts on.whyFails: memakai -s, padahal kalimat perintah nggak punya subjek yang perlu dicocokkan.

Putting on.whyFails: cuma menyebut kegiatan, bukan menyuruh orang melakukannya.

To put on.misconception: “to” + kata kerja dipakai untuk memberi perintah.
To put on.whyFails: memakai “to”, padahal perintah dimulai langsung dari kata kerjanya.

th.objective: ให้คำสั่งด้วยคำกริยารูปพื้นฐาน ใช้ 'Don't' + รูปพื้นฐานเพื่อห้าม และใช้ 'Let's' + รูปพื้นฐานเพื่อชวน ตัวอย่าง: 'It's cold outside. Put on your jacket!'
th.misconception: คุณเติมประธาน เติม -s เติม -ing หรือใส่ 'to' ในประโยคคำสั่ง หรือใช้แค่ 'not' เพื่อห้าม
th.reasoning: ดูว่าเป็นประโยคคำสั่ง → ดูว่าไม่มีประธาน → เลือกคำกริยาเปล่า ๆ
th.rule: คำสั่งใช้คำกริยารูปพื้นฐาน ('Open', 'Sit') คำห้ามใช้ 'Don't' + รูปพื้นฐาน ('Don't run') และคำชวนใช้ 'Let's' + รูปพื้นฐาน ('Let's go')
th.whyCorrect: นี่เป็นคำสั่งถึงคุณ จึงขึ้นต้นด้วยคำกริยารูปพื้นฐาน คือ 'Put on'
th.whyOthersFail: 'Puts on' เติม -s ส่วน 'Putting on' แค่บอกกิจกรรม และ 'To put on' ไม่ใช่ประโยคคำสั่ง
th.howToAvoid: เริ่มประโยคด้วยคำกริยาเลย ไม่มีประธาน ไม่เติม -s ไม่เติม -ing และไม่มี 'to'
th.memoryCue: ประโยคคำสั่งขึ้นต้นด้วยคำกริยาเปล่า ๆ เช่น 'Put on' หรือ 'Sit down'

Puts on.misconception: เติม -s ให้คำสั่ง
Puts on.whyFails: เติม -s แต่ประโยคคำสั่งไม่มีประธานให้ต้องเข้าคู่

Putting on.misconception: ใช้รูป -ing ออกคำสั่ง
Putting on.whyFails: แค่บอกชื่อกิจกรรม ไม่ได้สั่งให้ใครทำ

To put on.misconception: ใช้ 'to' + คำกริยาออกคำสั่ง
To put on.whyFails: มี 'to' แต่คำสั่งต้องขึ้นต้นด้วยคำกริยาเลย

en.objective: Show who owns something with 's for one owner and s' for plural owners ending in s. Example: The cat's bowl is empty. Can you feed it?
en.misconception: Learner puts two nouns side by side as in 'tas Sinta', writes -s without an apostrophe, or adds his or her after the name.
en.reasoning: identify the owner -> count one owner -> add 's to the owner
en.stem: The ___ bowl is empty. Can you feed it?

distractors.misconception: drops the marker of ownership entirely, lining up two nouns as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: It has no owner marker, so it reads like two nouns stuck together.

distractors.misconception: writes a plain -s ending that superficially resembles the possessive but loses the apostrophe
distractors.whyFails: Without an apostrophe it looks like 'many cats', not the owner.

distractors.misconception: inserting a duplicate owner pronoun after the name, marking possession twice
distractors.whyFails: It marks the owner twice; 's alone is enough.

explanation.whyCorrect: The bowl belongs to the cat, one owner, so we add 's to cat.
explanation.rule: Owner + 's + thing (Sinta's bag). Plural owner ending in s: add only an apostrophe (my parents' car). Plural without s: 's (children's).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Cat' has no owner marker, 'cats' looks like a plural, and 'cat its' marks the owner twice.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the owner first. One owner? Add 's. More than one and ending in s? Add only the apostrophe.
explanation.memoryCue: Owner + 's + thing: the cat's bowl.

id_.reasoning: cari pemiliknya → hitung pemiliknya satu → tambah 's pada pemiliknya
id_.rule: Pemilik + 's + barangnya (“Sinta's bag”). Pemilik jamak berakhiran s cukup ditambah apostrof (“my parents' car”). Jamak tanpa s tetap 's (“children's”).
id_.whyCorrect: Mangkuknya milik si kucing, satu pemilik, jadi “cat” ditambah 's.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Cat” nggak punya tanda pemilik, “cats” terbaca seperti bentuk jamak, dan “cat its” menandai pemilik dua kali.
id_.howToAvoid: Cari pemiliknya dulu. Satu pemilik? Tambah 's. Lebih dari satu dan berakhiran s? Cukup tambah apostrof.
id_.memoryCue: Pemilik + 's + barang: “the cat's bowl”.

th.objective: บอกความเป็นเจ้าของด้วย 's สำหรับเจ้าของคนเดียว และ s' สำหรับเจ้าของหลายคนที่ลงท้ายด้วย s ตัวอย่าง: 'My two brothers' room is next to mine.'
th.misconception: คุณวางคำนามสองคำติดกันเหมือน 'กระเป๋าสินตา' เขียน -s โดยไม่มีอะพอสทรอฟี หรือเติม 'his/her' หลังชื่อ
th.reasoning: นับจำนวนเจ้าของ → ดูตัว s ท้ายคำ → เติมแค่อะพอสทรอฟี
th.rule: เจ้าของ + 's + สิ่งของ ('Sinta's bag') ถ้าเจ้าของเป็นพหูพจน์ที่ลงท้ายด้วย s ให้เติมแค่อะพอสทรอฟี ส่วนพหูพจน์ที่ไม่มี s ยังใช้ 's ('children's')
th.whyCorrect: 'two brothers' เป็นพหูพจน์ที่ลงท้ายด้วย s แล้ว จึงเติมแค่อะพอสทรอฟีหลัง s
th.whyOthersFail: “brother's” ใช้กับพี่หรือน้องคนเดียว ส่วน “brother” ไม่มีทั้งเครื่องหมายพหูพจน์และเจ้าของ และ “brothers's” เติม s เกินมา
th.howToAvoid: หาเจ้าของก่อน ถ้ามีคนเดียวให้เติม 's ถ้ามีหลายคนและลงท้ายด้วย s ให้เติมแค่อะพอสทรอฟี

en.misconception: Learner puts two nouns side by side as in 'tas Sinta', writes -s without an apostrophe, or adds his or her after the name.
en.reasoning: identify the owners as children -> check that the word does not end in s -> add 's
en.stem: The ___ toys are all over the floor!

distractors.misconception: s added to a plural that does not take s
distractors.whyFails: It adds an s that 'children' never takes.

distractors.misconception: drops the marker of ownership entirely, lining up two nouns as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: It has no owner marker, so we cannot tell whose toys they are.

distractors.misconception: regular plural rule used for an irregular plural
distractors.whyFails: It is not a real word; the plural of child is children.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Children' is already plural but does not end in s, so we still add 's.
explanation.rule: Owner + 's + thing (Sinta's bag). Plural owner ending in s: add only an apostrophe (my parents' car). Plural without s: 's (children's).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Childrens'' adds a wrong s, 'children' has no owner marker, and 'childs'' is not a word.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the owner first. One owner? Add 's. More than one and ending in s? Add only the apostrophe.
explanation.memoryCue: Plural without s? Still add 's: children's, men's.

en.objective: Show who owns something with 's for one owner and s' for plural owners ending in s. Example: “Whose bag is this?” “It's Maya's.”
en.misconception: Learner puts two nouns side by side as in 'tas Sinta', writes -s without an apostrophe, or adds his or her after the name.
en.reasoning: check the question word whose -> identify the owner Maya -> add 's to the name
en.stem: “Whose bag is this?” “It's ___.”

distractors.misconception: owner named without any ownership marker
distractors.whyFails: It just names the person; it does not say the bag is hers.

distractors.misconception: writes a plain -s ending that superficially resembles the possessive but loses the apostrophe
distractors.whyFails: Without the apostrophe it is not an owner form.

distractors.misconception: of + name used for a person's belongings
distractors.whyFails: It copies 'punya Maya'; English uses 's for a person's things.

explanation.whyCorrect: The answer names the owner, Maya, so we add 's to her name, even with no noun after it.
explanation.rule: Owner + 's + thing (Sinta's bag). Plural owner ending in s: add only an apostrophe (my parents' car). Plural without s: 's (children's).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Maya' has no owner marker, 'Mayas' has no apostrophe, and 'of Maya' is not how English shows a person's things.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the owner first. One owner? Add 's. More than one and ending in s? Add only the apostrophe.
explanation.memoryCue: It's Maya's = it belongs to Maya.

en.objective: Use would like to ask for things politely and Would you like…? to offer. Example: I would like to book a table for four, please.
en.misconception: Learner asks about taste with 'Do you like' when offering, or puts -ing or no to after would like.
en.reasoning: notice would like before the blank -> check that a verb follows -> add to before the base verb
en.stem: I would like ___ a table for four, please.

distractors.misconception: to dropped after would like
distractors.whyFails: It has no to, but a verb after would like needs to.

distractors.misconception: -ing form used after would like
distractors.whyFails: It adds -ing, but would like takes to + the base verb.

distractors.misconception: mixes the to-infinitive and the -ing ending into one broken shape
distractors.whyFails: It mixes to with -ing; after to, the verb stays in its base form.

explanation.whyCorrect: After would like, another verb needs to, so: would like to book.
explanation.rule: Ask politely: I would like + thing, or + to + verb. Offer: Would you like + thing or to + verb? Someone else: would like me to + verb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Book' has no to, 'booking' adds -ing, and 'to booking' mixes to with -ing.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ordering or offering? Use would like. If a verb comes next, put to before it.
explanation.memoryCue: Would like + to + verb: I'd like to book, I'd like to go.

id_.objective: Pakai “would like” untuk meminta dengan sopan dan “Would you like…?” untuk menawarkan. Contoh: “I would like to book a table for four, please.”
id_.misconception: Kamu menawarkan dengan “Do you like” yang sebenarnya menanyakan selera, atau memakai -ing atau lupa “to” sesudah “would like”.
id_.reasoning: lihat “would like” sebelum titik-titik → cek bahwa sesudahnya kata kerja → tambah “to” sebelum bentuk dasar
id_.rule: Meminta: “I would like” + benda, atau + “to” + kata kerja. Menawarkan: “Would you like…?”. Menyuruh orang lain: “would like me to” + kata kerja.
id_.whyCorrect: Sesudah “would like”, kata kerja berikutnya butuh “to”, jadi “would like to book”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Book” nggak pakai “to”, “booking” menambah -ing, dan “to booking” mencampur “to” dengan -ing.
id_.howToAvoid: Lagi memesan atau menawarkan? Pakai “would like”. Kalau sesudahnya kata kerja, taruh “to” di depannya.
id_.memoryCue: “Would like” + “to” + kata kerja: “I'd like to book”.

book.whyFails: nggak memakai “to”, padahal kata kerja sesudah “would like” butuh “to”.

booking.whyFails: memakai -ing, padahal “would like” diikuti “to” + bentuk dasar.

to booking.whyFails: mencampur “to” dengan -ing, padahal sesudah “to” kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar.

th.objective: ใช้ 'would like' เพื่อขออย่างสุภาพ และใช้ 'Would you like…?' เพื่อเสนอ ตัวอย่าง: 'I would like to book a table for four, please.'
th.misconception: คุณใช้ 'Do you like' ซึ่งถามเรื่องความชอบเวลาจะเสนอ หรือใช้ -ing หรือลืม 'to' หลัง 'would like'
th.reasoning: เห็น 'would like' หน้าช่องว่าง → ดูว่าตามด้วยคำกริยา → เติม 'to' หน้ารูปพื้นฐาน
th.rule: ขออย่างสุภาพใช้ 'I would like' + สิ่งของ หรือ + 'to' + คำกริยา ถ้าจะเสนอใช้ 'Would you like…?' ถ้าอยากให้คนอื่นทำใช้ 'would like me to' + คำกริยา
th.whyCorrect: หลัง 'would like' คำกริยาตัวต่อไปต้องมี 'to' จึงเป็น 'would like to book'
th.whyOthersFail: คำว่า 'book' ขาด 'to' ส่วน 'booking' เติม -ing และ 'to booking' เอา 'to' กับ -ing มาผสมกันซึ่งผิด
th.howToAvoid: ถ้ากำลังสั่งหรือเสนอ ให้ใช้ 'would like' และถ้าตามด้วยคำกริยา ให้ใส่ 'to' ข้างหน้า
th.memoryCue: เวลาขออย่างสุภาพแล้วตามด้วยคำกริยา ให้ใส่ 'to' เสมอ เช่น 'I'd like to go'

book.whyFails: ไม่มี 'to' แต่คำกริยาหลัง 'would like' ต้องมี 'to'

booking.misconception: ใช้รูป -ing หลังคำขออย่างสุภาพ 'would like'
booking.whyFails: เติม -ing แต่ 'would like' ต้องตามด้วย 'to' + รูปพื้นฐาน

to booking.whyFails: ผสม 'to' กับ -ing แต่หลัง 'to' คำกริยาต้องเป็นรูปพื้นฐาน

en.misconception: Learner asks about taste with 'Do you like' when offering, or puts -ing or no to after would like.
en.reasoning: notice I made it myself -> identify the question as an offer -> choose the word for a polite offer
en.stem: ___ you like some cake? I made it myself!

distractors.misconception: stating a general preference in casual flat form instead of the polite request formula
distractors.whyFails: It asks what you like in general, not whether you want cake now.

distractors.misconception: be used with like in an offer
distractors.whyFails: It is a be word, and be words cannot go with like.

distractors.misconception: will used for a polite offer
distractors.whyFails: It talks about the future, but polite offers use a different word.

explanation.whyCorrect: It is an offer, and polite offers use Would you like…?
explanation.rule: Ask politely: I would like + thing, or + to + verb. Offer: Would you like + thing or to + verb? Someone else: would like me to + verb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Do you like' asks about taste in general, 'Are' cannot go with like, and 'Will' is not used for offers like this.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ordering or offering? Use would like. If a verb comes next, put to before it.
explanation.memoryCue: Offering something? Would you like…?

Do.whyFails: menanyakan selera secara umum, bukan menawarkan kue sekarang.

en.objective: Use like, love, hate, and enjoy + verb-ing to talk about activities you like or dislike. Example: My little sister loves dancing to K-pop songs.
en.misconception: Learner puts the base verb right after like or enjoy, as in 'suka main', or spells the -ing form wrongly.
en.reasoning: notice loves before the blank -> add -ing to the verb -> remove the final e
en.stem: My little sister loves ___ to K-pop songs.

distractors.misconception: final e kept before -ing
distractors.whyFails: It keeps the e, but the e drops before -ing.

distractors.misconception: following the feeling verb with a bare infinitive, chaining verbs directly as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: It has no -ing, but after loves the verb needs it.

distractors.misconception: mixes the to-infinitive and the -ing ending into one broken shape
distractors.whyFails: It mixes to with -ing in one form.

explanation.whyCorrect: After loves we use -ing, and dance drops its e before -ing.
explanation.rule: Like, love, hate, enjoy + verb-ing (I love swimming). Enjoy always takes -ing. Spelling: swim, swimming; dance, dancing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Danceing' keeps the e, 'dance' has no -ing, and 'to dancing' mixes to with -ing.
explanation.howToAvoid: After a feeling verb, give the next verb -ing and check the spelling.
explanation.memoryCue: The final e goes before -ing: dance, dancing; make, making.

en.objective: Choose the present simple for habits and the present continuous for things happening now. Example: Dina usually walks to school, but today she is taking the bus.
en.misconception: Learner picks the verb form without looking at the time words, since 'setiap hari' and 'sekarang' do not change the verb.
en.reasoning: find the time word usually -> identify it as a habit -> choose the habit form for she
en.stem: Dina usually ___ to school, but today she is taking the bus.

distractors.misconception: progressive form used for a habit
distractors.whyFails: It is for now, but usually shows a habit.

distractors.misconception: missing subject-verb agreement / bare form
distractors.whyFails: It forgets -s, but Dina is she.

distractors.misconception: past tense used for a timeless fact
distractors.whyFails: It is past, but usually talks about her habit now.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Usually' shows a habit, and Dina is she, so: walks.
explanation.rule: Habit (every day, usually): present simple. Happening now (now, look!): a be form + -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Is walking' is for now, 'walk' forgets -s, and 'walked' is past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Circle the time word first: a habit word or a now word?
explanation.memoryCue: Usually = habit = walks. Today = now = is taking.

id_.objective: Pilih present simple untuk kebiasaan dan present continuous untuk kejadian yang sedang berlangsung. Contoh: “Dina usually walks to school, but today she is taking the bus.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memilih bentuk kata kerja tanpa melihat kata waktunya, karena “setiap hari” dan “sekarang” nggak mengubah kata kerja dalam bahasa Indonesia.
id_.reasoning: cari kata waktunya, “usually” → pastikan itu kebiasaan → pilih bentuk kebiasaan untuk “she”
id_.rule: Untuk kebiasaan (“every day”, “usually”) pakai present simple. Untuk yang sedang terjadi (“now”, “look!”) pakai bentuk “be” + -ing.
id_.whyCorrect: “Usually” menunjukkan kebiasaan, dan Dina sama dengan “she”, jadi “walks”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Is walking” untuk kejadian sekarang, “walk” lupa -s, dan “walked” bentuk lampau.
id_.howToAvoid: Lingkari kata waktunya dulu: kata kebiasaan atau kata “sekarang”?
id_.memoryCue: “Usually” = kebiasaan = “walks”. “Today” = sekarang = “is taking”.

walked.whyFails: bentuk lampau, padahal “usually” membicarakan kebiasaannya sekarang.

takes.whyFails: เป็นรูปกิจวัตรของคนเดียว แต่นักเรียนหลายคนกำลังทำอยู่ตอนนี้

en.objective: Choose the present simple for habits and the present continuous for things happening now. Example: My mum doesn't drink coffee. She only drinks tea.
en.misconception: Learner picks the verb form without looking at the time words, since 'setiap hari' and 'sekarang' do not change the verb.
en.reasoning: check the second sentence -> identify it as a habit -> choose the habit negative for she
en.stem: My mum ___ coffee. She only drinks tea.

distractors.misconception: progressive negative used for a general habit
distractors.whyFails: It is only about this moment, but the sentence is about her habit.

distractors.misconception: don't used with he, she, or it
distractors.whyFails: It is for I, you, we, and they, but my mum is she.

distractors.misconception: not used without a helper verb in a negative
distractors.whyFails: It has no helper word; this negative needs doesn't.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'She only drinks tea' is a general habit, so the negative is doesn't drink.
explanation.rule: Habit (every day, usually): present simple. Happening now (now, look!): a be form + -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Isn't drinking' is only about now, 'don't drink' is for I, you, we, and they, and 'not drinks' has no helper word.
explanation.howToAvoid: Circle the time word first: a habit word or a now word?
explanation.memoryCue: A habit, not just now: she doesn't drink.

id_.objective: Pilih present simple untuk kebiasaan dan present continuous untuk kejadian yang sedang berlangsung. Contoh: “My mum doesn't drink coffee. She only drinks tea.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memilih bentuk kata kerja tanpa melihat kata waktunya, karena “setiap hari” dan “sekarang” nggak mengubah kata kerja dalam bahasa Indonesia.
id_.reasoning: lihat kalimat kedua → pastikan itu kebiasaan → pilih bentuk negatif kebiasaan untuk “she”
id_.rule: Untuk kebiasaan (“every day”, “usually”) pakai present simple. Untuk yang sedang terjadi (“now”, “look!”) pakai bentuk “be” + -ing.
id_.whyCorrect: “She only drinks tea” adalah kebiasaan umum, jadi bentuk negatifnya “doesn't drink”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Isn't drinking” cuma soal saat ini, “don't drink” untuk “I”, “you”, “we”, dan “they”, dan “not drinks” nggak punya kata bantu.
id_.howToAvoid: Lingkari kata waktunya dulu: kata kebiasaan atau kata “sekarang”?
id_.memoryCue: Kebiasaan, bukan cuma saat ini: “she doesn't drink”.

isn't drinking.misconception: bentuk negatif yang sedang berlangsung dipakai untuk kebiasaan umum.
isn't drinking.whyFails: cuma soal saat ini, padahal kalimatnya membicarakan kebiasaannya.

don't drink.whyFails: untuk “I”, “you”, “we”, dan “they”, padahal “my mum” sama dengan “she”.

not drinks.misconception: “not” dipakai tanpa kata bantu di kalimat negatif.
not drinks.whyFails: nggak punya kata bantu, padahal kalimat negatif ini butuh “doesn't”.

th.objective: เลือก present simple สำหรับกิจวัตร และ present continuous สำหรับสิ่งที่กำลังเกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ ตัวอย่าง: 'My mum doesn't drink coffee. She only drinks tea.'
th.misconception: คุณเลือกรูปคำกริยาโดยไม่ดูคำบอกเวลา เพราะคำว่า 'ทุกวัน' กับ 'ตอนนี้' ไม่ได้เปลี่ยนรูปคำกริยาในภาษาไทย
th.reasoning: ดูประโยคที่สอง → ดูว่าเป็นกิจวัตร → เลือกรูปปฏิเสธแบบกิจวัตรของ 'she'
th.rule: ถ้าเป็นกิจวัตรที่ทำเป็นประจำ เช่นมีคำว่า 'every day' ให้ใช้ present simple ถ้ากำลังเกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ เช่นมีคำว่า 'now' ให้ใช้รูป 'be' + -ing
th.whyCorrect: 'She only drinks tea' เป็นกิจวัตรทั่วไป รูปปฏิเสธจึงเป็น 'doesn't drink'
th.whyOthersFail: 'isn't drinking' พูดถึงแค่ตอนนี้ ส่วน 'don't drink' ใช้กับ 'I', 'you', 'we', 'they' และ 'not drinks' ไม่มีกริยาช่วย
th.howToAvoid: วงคำบอกเวลาก่อนว่าเป็นคำบอกกิจวัตรหรือคำที่บอกว่าตอนนี้
th.memoryCue: ถ้าเป็นกิจวัตร ไม่ใช่แค่ตอนนี้ ให้ใช้ 'she doesn't drink'

isn't drinking.misconception: ใช้รูปปฏิเสธแบบกำลังทำกับกิจวัตรทั่วไป
isn't drinking.whyFails: พูดถึงแค่ตอนนี้ แต่ประโยคนี้พูดถึงกิจวัตรของเธอ

don't drink.misconception: ใช้ 'don't' กับประธานที่เป็นเขาหรือเธอคนเดียว
don't drink.whyFails: ใช้กับหลายคนหรือกับ 'I' และ 'you' แต่แม่ของฉันเป็นคนเดียว

not drinks.misconception: ใช้ 'not' โดยไม่มีกริยาช่วยในประโยคปฏิเสธ
not drinks.whyFails: ไม่มีกริยาช่วย แต่ประโยคปฏิเสธนี้ต้องใช้ 'doesn't'

en.objective: Choose the present simple for habits and the present continuous for things happening now. Example: Why are you carrying an umbrella? It isn't raining.
en.misconception: Learner picks the verb form without looking at the time words, since 'setiap hari' and 'sekarang' do not change the verb.
en.reasoning: notice it isn't raining -> identify the action as happening now -> place are before you and add -ing
en.stem: Why ___ an umbrella? It isn't raining.

distractors.misconception: statement order used for a question
distractors.whyFails: It keeps statement order, so it is not a question.

distractors.misconception: -ing missing after am, is, or are
distractors.whyFails: It forgets -ing after are.

distractors.misconception: do mixed with an -ing verb
distractors.whyFails: It mixes do with -ing; an -ing verb needs a be word.

explanation.whyCorrect: It is happening now, so the question uses are + you + -ing, which gives are you carrying.
explanation.rule: Habit (every day, usually): present simple. Happening now (now, look!): a be form + -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'You are carrying' keeps statement order, 'are you carry' forgets -ing, and 'do you carrying' mixes do with -ing.
explanation.howToAvoid: Circle the time word first: a habit word or a now word?
explanation.memoryCue: A question about now: Why are you + -ing?

id_.objective: Pilih present simple untuk kebiasaan dan present continuous untuk kejadian yang sedang berlangsung. Contoh: “Why are you carrying an umbrella? It isn't raining.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memilih bentuk kata kerja tanpa melihat kata waktunya, karena “setiap hari” dan “sekarang” nggak mengubah kata kerja dalam bahasa Indonesia.
id_.reasoning: perhatikan “It isn't raining” → pastikan kejadiannya sekarang → taruh “are” sebelum “you” dan tambah -ing
id_.rule: Untuk kebiasaan (“every day”, “usually”) pakai present simple. Untuk yang sedang terjadi (“now”, “look!”) pakai bentuk “be” + -ing.
id_.whyCorrect: Kejadiannya sekarang, jadi kalimat tanyanya “are” + “you” + -ing, yaitu “are you carrying”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “You are carrying” memakai susunan kalimat berita, “are you carry” lupa -ing, dan “do you carrying” mencampur “do” dengan -ing.
id_.howToAvoid: Lingkari kata waktunya dulu: kata kebiasaan atau kata “sekarang”?
id_.memoryCue: Tanya soal sekarang: “Why are you” + -ing?

you are carrying.misconception: susunan kalimat berita dipakai untuk kalimat tanya.
you are carrying.whyFails: memakai susunan kalimat berita, jadi belum jadi pertanyaan.

are you carry.whyFails: lupa -ing, padahal sesudah “are” kata kerjanya butuh -ing.

do you carrying.misconception: kata bantu “do” dicampur dengan kata kerja -ing.
do you carrying.whyFails: mencampur “do” dengan -ing, padahal kata kerja -ing butuh bentuk “be”.

th.objective: เลือก present simple สำหรับกิจวัตร และ present continuous สำหรับสิ่งที่กำลังเกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ ตัวอย่าง: 'Why are you carrying an umbrella? It isn't raining.'
th.misconception: คุณเลือกรูปคำกริยาโดยไม่ดูคำบอกเวลา เพราะคำว่า 'ทุกวัน' กับ 'ตอนนี้' ไม่ได้เปลี่ยนรูปคำกริยาในภาษาไทย
th.reasoning: สังเกต 'It isn't raining' → ดูว่าเกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ → วาง 'are' ไว้หน้า 'you' และเติม -ing
th.rule: ถ้าเป็นกิจวัตรที่ทำเป็นประจำ เช่นมีคำว่า 'every day' ให้ใช้ present simple ถ้ากำลังเกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ เช่นมีคำว่า 'now' ให้ใช้รูป 'be' + -ing
th.whyCorrect: เป็นสิ่งที่เกิดขึ้นตอนนี้ คำถามจึงใช้ 'are' + 'you' + -ing คือ 'are you carrying'
th.whyOthersFail: 'you are carrying' ใช้ลำดับประโยคบอกเล่า ส่วนอีกสองตัวเลือกลืมเติม -ing หรือเอา 'do' มาผสมกับ -ing
th.howToAvoid: วงคำบอกเวลาก่อนว่าเป็นคำบอกกิจวัตรหรือคำที่บอกว่าตอนนี้
th.memoryCue: ถ้าถามเรื่องตอนนี้ ให้ใช้ 'Why are you' + -ing

you are carrying.misconception: ใช้ลำดับของประโยคบอกเล่ากับคำถาม
you are carrying.whyFails: ใช้ลำดับของประโยคบอกเล่า จึงยังไม่เป็นคำถาม

are you carry.misconception: ลืมเติม -ing หลังรูป 'be'
are you carry.whyFails: ลืมเติม -ing ทั้งที่หลัง 'are' ต้องเติม -ing

do you carrying.misconception: ผสม 'do' กับคำกริยาเติม -ing
do you carrying.whyFails: ผสม 'do' กับ -ing แต่คำกริยา -ing ต้องใช้รูป 'be'

en.objective: Choose must or have to for rules, can for permission, mustn't for 'not allowed', and don't have to for 'not necessary'. Example: You mustn't use your phone during the test. It's against the rules.
en.misconception: Learner mixes up mustn't (not allowed) and don't have to (not necessary), since 'nggak harus' and 'nggak boleh' sound close.
en.reasoning: notice against the rules -> identify it as a ban -> choose the word for not allowed
en.stem: You ___ use your phone during the test. It's against the rules.

distractors.misconception: don't have to used for a ban
distractors.whyFails: It means 'not necessary', so it sounds like a free choice, not a ban.

distractors.misconception: must used where the rule forbids the action
distractors.whyFails: It means you have to use your phone, the opposite of the rule.

distractors.misconception: can used for something the rules forbid
distractors.whyFails: It gives permission, but the rules say no.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Against the rules' means it is not allowed, so we use mustn't.
explanation.rule: Must, have to = necessary. Can = allowed. Mustn't = not allowed. Don't have to = not necessary, you may choose.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Don't have to' means it is not necessary, 'must' means you have to use it, and 'can' gives permission.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask yourself: is it a rule, a permission, a ban, or a free choice?
explanation.memoryCue: Against the rules = mustn't = dilarang.

id_.objective: Pilih “must”/“have to” untuk aturan, “can” untuk izin, “mustn't” untuk larangan, dan “don't have to” untuk “nggak perlu”. Contoh: “You mustn't use your phone during the test. It's against the rules.”
id_.misconception: Kamu tertukar antara “mustn't” (dilarang) dan “don't have to” (nggak perlu), karena “nggak harus” dan “nggak boleh” terdengar mirip.
id_.reasoning: perhatikan “against the rules” → pastikan itu larangan → pilih kata untuk “dilarang”
id_.rule: “Must”/“have to” = wajib. “Can” = boleh. “Mustn't” = dilarang. “Don't have to” = nggak wajib, boleh memilih.
id_.whyCorrect: “Against the rules” artinya dilarang, jadi pakai “mustn't”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Don't have to” artinya nggak perlu, “must” artinya wajib memakainya, dan “can” memberi izin.
id_.howToAvoid: Tanya dirimu: ini aturan, izin, larangan, atau pilihan bebas?
id_.memoryCue: Melanggar aturan = “mustn't” = dilarang.

don't have to.misconception: “don't have to” (nggak perlu) dipakai untuk larangan.
don't have to.whyFails: artinya “nggak perlu”, jadi terdengar seperti pilihan bebas, bukan larangan.

must.misconception: “must” (wajib) dipakai untuk hal yang justru dilarang.
must.whyFails: artinya wajib memakai ponsel, kebalikan dari aturannya.

can.misconception: “can” (boleh) dipakai untuk hal yang dilarang aturan.

th.objective: เลือก 'must' หรือ 'have to' สำหรับกฎ 'can' สำหรับการอนุญาต 'mustn't' สำหรับข้อห้าม และ 'don't have to' สำหรับสิ่งที่ไม่จำเป็น ตัวอย่าง: 'You mustn't use your phone during the test. It's against the rules.'
th.misconception: คุณสับสนระหว่าง 'mustn't' ที่แปลว่าห้าม กับ 'don't have to' ที่แปลว่าไม่จำเป็น
th.reasoning: สังเกต 'against the rules' → ดูว่าเป็นข้อห้าม → เลือกคำที่แปลว่าห้าม
th.rule: 'must' หรือ 'have to' แปลว่าต้องทำ 'can' แปลว่าทำได้ 'mustn't' แปลว่าห้ามทำ และ 'don't have to' แปลว่าไม่จำเป็นต้องทำ
th.whyCorrect: 'against the rules' แปลว่าผิดกฎ จึงเป็นสิ่งที่ห้ามทำ และต้องใช้ 'mustn't'
th.whyOthersFail: 'don't have to' แปลว่าไม่จำเป็น ส่วน 'must' แปลว่าต้องใช้ และ 'can' แปลว่าอนุญาต
th.howToAvoid: ถามตัวเองว่านี่เป็นกฎ การอนุญาต ข้อห้าม หรือทางเลือก
th.memoryCue: ผิดกฎใช้ 'mustn't' ซึ่งแปลว่าห้าม

don't have to.misconception: ใช้ 'don't have to' ที่แปลว่าไม่จำเป็นกับข้อห้าม
don't have to.whyFails: แปลว่าไม่จำเป็น จึงฟังเหมือนเป็นทางเลือก ไม่ใช่ข้อห้าม

must.misconception: ใช้ 'must' ที่แปลว่าต้องทำ กับสิ่งที่ถูกห้าม
must.whyFails: แปลว่าต้องใช้โทรศัพท์ ซึ่งตรงข้ามกับกฎ

can.misconception: ใช้ 'can' ที่แปลว่าทำได้ กับสิ่งที่กฎห้าม
can.whyFails: เป็นการอนุญาต แต่กฎห้ามไว้

en.objective: Choose must or have to for rules, can for permission, mustn't for 'not allowed', and don't have to for 'not necessary'. Example: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we don't have to go to school.
en.misconception: Learner mixes up mustn't (not allowed) and don't have to (not necessary), since 'nggak harus' and 'nggak boleh' sound close.
en.reasoning: notice a holiday -> decide if going is banned or just not necessary -> choose the words for not necessary
en.stem: Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ___ go to school.

distractors.misconception: treats 'mustn't' as the negation of obligation rather than prohibition
distractors.whyFails: It means going to school is not allowed, which is too strong for a holiday.

distractors.misconception: have to used when there is no need
distractors.whyFails: It means we must go, but it is a holiday.

distractors.misconception: confuses lack of requirement with lack of permission/ability
distractors.whyFails: It means we are not able or not allowed, but nobody forbids it.

explanation.whyCorrect: A holiday means going to school is not necessary, so we use don't have to.
explanation.rule: Must, have to = necessary. Can = allowed. Mustn't = not allowed. Don't have to = not necessary, you may choose.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed, 'have to' means it is necessary, and 'can't' means we are not able or allowed.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask yourself: is it a rule, a permission, a ban, or a free choice?
explanation.memoryCue: No need = don't have to. Not allowed = mustn't.

id_.objective: Pilih “must”/“have to” untuk aturan, “can” untuk izin, “mustn't” untuk larangan, dan “don't have to” untuk “nggak perlu”. Contoh: “Tomorrow is a holiday, so we don't have to go to school.”
id_.misconception: Kamu tertukar antara “mustn't” (dilarang) dan “don't have to” (nggak perlu), karena “nggak harus” dan “nggak boleh” terdengar mirip.
id_.reasoning: perhatikan “a holiday” → putuskan ke sekolah itu dilarang atau cuma nggak perlu → pilih kata untuk “nggak perlu”
id_.rule: “Must”/“have to” = wajib. “Can” = boleh. “Mustn't” = dilarang. “Don't have to” = nggak wajib, boleh memilih.
id_.whyCorrect: Hari libur artinya nggak perlu ke sekolah, jadi pakai “don't have to”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Mustn't” artinya dilarang, “have to” artinya wajib, dan “can't” artinya nggak bisa atau nggak boleh.
id_.howToAvoid: Tanya dirimu: ini aturan, izin, larangan, atau pilihan bebas?
id_.memoryCue: Nggak perlu = “don't have to”. Dilarang = “mustn't”.

mustn't.whyFails: artinya dilarang ke sekolah, padahal libur cuma berarti nggak perlu.

have to.misconception: “have to” (wajib) dipakai saat nggak ada keharusan.
have to.whyFails: artinya wajib pergi, padahal besok libur.

can't.misconception: “can't” dipakai untuk hal yang cuma nggak perlu.
can't.whyFails: artinya nggak bisa atau nggak boleh, padahal nggak ada yang melarang.

th.objective: เลือก 'must' หรือ 'have to' สำหรับกฎ 'can' สำหรับการอนุญาต 'mustn't' สำหรับข้อห้าม และ 'don't have to' สำหรับสิ่งที่ไม่จำเป็น ตัวอย่าง: 'Tomorrow is a holiday, so we don't have to go to school.'

en.objective: Choose must or have to for rules, can for permission, mustn't for 'not allowed', and don't have to for 'not necessary'. Example: “Can I borrow your pen?” “Sure, here you are.”
en.misconception: Learner mixes up mustn't (not allowed) and don't have to (not necessary), since 'nggak harus' and 'nggak boleh' sound close.
en.reasoning: check the answer sure -> identify the question as asking permission -> choose the word for asking permission
en.stem: “___ I borrow your pen?” “Sure, here you are.”

distractors.misconception: must used to ask for permission
distractors.whyFails: It asks whether you are required to, not whether you are allowed.

distractors.misconception: have used without to in a question
distractors.whyFails: It would need to and would mean 'must', so it cannot ask for permission.

distractors.misconception: do used to ask for permission
distractors.whyFails: It asks about a habit, not for permission.

explanation.whyCorrect: Asking for permission uses Can I…?, and the answer 'Sure' gives it.
explanation.rule: Must, have to = necessary. Can = allowed. Mustn't = not allowed. Don't have to = not necessary, you may choose.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Must' asks if it is necessary, and 'Have' and 'Do' cannot ask for permission like this.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask yourself: is it a rule, a permission, a ban, or a free choice?
explanation.memoryCue: Asking permission: Can I…? May I…?

Must.whyFails: menanyakan apakah kamu wajib, bukan apakah kamu boleh.

th.misconception: คุณสับสนระหว่าง 'mustn't' ที่แปลว่าห้าม กับ 'don't have to' ที่แปลว่าไม่จำเป็น
th.reasoning: ดูคำตอบ 'Sure' → ดูว่าเป็นการขออนุญาต → เลือกคำที่ใช้ขออนุญาต

th.howToAvoid: ถามตัวเองว่านี่เป็นกฎ การอนุญาต ข้อห้าม หรือทางเลือก

en.reasoning: notice it's the law -> identify it as a rule -> choose the words for necessary
en.stem: In Indonesia, drivers ___ drive on the left. It's the law.

distractors.misconception: don't have to used for a law
distractors.whyFails: It makes driving on the left a free choice, but it is the law.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as ability/permission
distractors.whyFails: It only says drivers are allowed to, but the law requires it.

distractors.misconception: mustn't used for something that is required
distractors.whyFails: It bans driving on the left, the opposite of the law.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'It's the law' means it is necessary, so drivers have to drive on the left.
explanation.rule: Must, have to = necessary. Can = allowed. Mustn't = not allowed. Don't have to = not necessary, you may choose.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Don't have to' makes it a free choice, 'can' only gives permission, and 'mustn't' bans it.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask yourself: is it a rule, a permission, a ban, or a free choice?
explanation.memoryCue: The law says so = have to or must.

en.objective: Use if + present, present for things that are always true, and if + present, will + verb for one real future result. Example: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go to the beach.
en.misconception: Learner puts will after if because the event is in the future, or uses the past for a fact that is always true.
en.reasoning: find the if part -> recall that the if part uses the present -> add -s for it
en.stem: If it ___ tomorrow, we won't go to the beach.

distractors.misconception: will used after if
distractors.whyFails: It puts will after if, but the if part uses the present.

distractors.misconception: uses simple past for an explicitly future consequence
distractors.whyFails: It is past, but tomorrow is in the future.

distractors.misconception: missing subject-verb agreement / bare form
distractors.whyFails: It forgets -s, but the subject is it.

explanation.whyCorrect: After if we use the present simple, even for tomorrow, so: rains.
explanation.rule: Always true: If + present, present (If you heat ice, it melts). One future result: If + present, will + verb. No will after if.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will rain' puts will after if, 'rained' is past, and 'rain' forgets -s for it.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is it always true, or one future event? Then check that no will follows if.
explanation.memoryCue: If + present, will + verb: If it rains, we will stay.

id_.objective: Pakai “if” + present, present untuk hal yang selalu benar, dan “if” + present, “will” + kata kerja untuk satu akibat nyata di masa depan. Contoh: “If it rains tomorrow, we won't go to the beach.”
id_.misconception: Kamu menaruh “will” sesudah “if” karena kejadiannya nanti, atau memakai bentuk lampau untuk fakta yang selalu benar.
id_.reasoning: cari bagian “if” → ingat bagian “if” pakai present → tambah -s untuk “it”
id_.rule: Selalu benar: “If” + present, present (“If you heat ice, it melts”). Akibat di masa depan: “If” + present, “will” + kata kerja. Sesudah “if” jangan pakai “will”.
id_.whyCorrect: Sesudah “if” pakai present simple, walaupun kejadiannya besok, jadi “rains”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Will rain” menaruh “will” sesudah “if”, “rained” bentuk lampau, dan “rain” lupa -s untuk “it”.
id_.howToAvoid: Tanya: ini selalu benar, atau satu kejadian nanti? Lalu pastikan nggak ada “will” sesudah “if”.
id_.memoryCue: “If” + present, “will” + kata kerja: “If it rains, we will stay”.

will rain.whyFails: menaruh “will” sesudah “if”, padahal bagian “if” memakai present.

rained.misconception: bentuk lampau dipakai untuk hari esok.
rained.whyFails: bentuk lampau, padahal “tomorrow” masih di masa depan.

th.objective: ใช้ 'if' + ปัจจุบัน ตามด้วยปัจจุบัน กับสิ่งที่จริงเสมอ และใช้ 'if' + ปัจจุบัน ตามด้วย 'will' + คำกริยา กับผลที่จะเกิดจริงในอนาคต ตัวอย่าง: 'If it rains tomorrow, we won't go to the beach.'
th.misconception: คุณใส่ 'will' หลัง 'if' เพราะเป็นเรื่องในอนาคต หรือใช้รูปอดีตกับความจริงที่เป็นจริงเสมอ
th.reasoning: หาส่วนที่มี 'if' → นึกว่าส่วน 'if' ใช้ปัจจุบัน → เติม -s ให้ 'it'
th.rule: ถ้าจริงเสมอ ใช้ 'If' + ปัจจุบัน แล้วตามด้วยปัจจุบัน ('If you heat ice, it melts') ถ้าเป็นผลในอนาคต ใช้ 'If' + ปัจจุบัน แล้วตามด้วย 'will' + คำกริยา และห้ามใช้ 'will' หลัง 'if'
th.whyCorrect: หลัง 'if' ใช้ present simple แม้จะพูดถึงพรุ่งนี้ จึงใช้ 'rains'
th.whyOthersFail: 'will rain' ใส่ 'will' หลัง 'if' ส่วน 'rained' เป็นรูปอดีต และ 'rain' ลืมเติม -s ให้ 'it'
th.howToAvoid: ถามตัวเองว่าจริงเสมอหรือเป็นเหตุการณ์ในอนาคตครั้งเดียว แล้วดูว่าไม่มี 'will' หลัง 'if'
th.memoryCue: หลัง 'if' ใช้ปัจจุบัน แล้วค่อยใช้ 'will' ในอีกครึ่งประโยค

en.misconception: Learner puts will after if because the event is in the future, or uses the past for a fact that is always true.
en.reasoning: identify the sentence as a fact that is always true -> recall present + present for facts -> keep the verb in the present
en.stem: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.

distractors.misconception: real condition treated as hypothetical
distractors.whyFails: It is for imagined situations, but this really happens.

distractors.misconception: past tense used for a timeless fact
distractors.whyFails: It is past, but this fact is true at any time.

distractors.misconception: reduces the sentence to a fragment: an -ing form with no finite verb to carry the tense
distractors.whyFails: It cannot stand alone as the verb of the sentence.

explanation.whyCorrect: Red and blue always make purple. A fact that is always true uses the present, so: get.
explanation.rule: Always true: If + present, present (If you heat ice, it melts). One future result: If + present, will + verb. No will after if.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Got' is past, 'would get' is for imagined situations, and 'getting' cannot stand alone as the verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is it always true, or one future event? Then check that no will follows if.
explanation.memoryCue: Always true? Present + present.

en.objective: Use if + present, present for things that are always true, and if + present, will + verb for one real future result. Example: Hurry up! If you don't leave now, you will miss the bus.
en.misconception: Learner puts will after if because the event is in the future, or uses the past for a fact that is always true.
en.reasoning: notice hurry up and now -> identify the result as one future event -> combine will with the base verb
en.stem: Hurry up! If you don't leave now, you ___ the bus.

distractors.misconception: drops the future marker entirely, defaulting to present simple
distractors.whyFails: It has no will, so it sounds like a general fact, not a warning about this bus.

distractors.misconception: uses simple past for an explicitly future consequence
distractors.whyFails: It is past, but the bus has not left yet.

distractors.misconception: -ing form used after will
distractors.whyFails: It adds -ing, but after will the verb stays in its base form.

explanation.whyCorrect: This is a warning about one future result, so the result part uses will + the base verb.
explanation.rule: Always true: If + present, present (If you heat ice, it melts). One future result: If + present, will + verb. No will after if.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Miss' sounds like a general fact, 'missed' is past, and 'will missing' adds -ing after will.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is it always true, or one future event? Then check that no will follows if.
explanation.memoryCue: A warning about later: If you…, you will…

id_.objective: Pakai “if” + present, present untuk hal yang selalu benar, dan “if” + present, “will” + kata kerja untuk satu akibat nyata di masa depan. Contoh: “Hurry up! If you don't leave now, you will miss the bus.”
id_.misconception: Kamu menaruh “will” sesudah “if” karena kejadiannya nanti, atau memakai bentuk lampau untuk fakta yang selalu benar.
id_.reasoning: perhatikan “Hurry up!” dan “now” → pastikan akibatnya satu kejadian nanti → gabungkan “will” dengan kata kerja dasar
id_.rule: Selalu benar: “If” + present, present (“If you heat ice, it melts”). Akibat di masa depan: “If” + present, “will” + kata kerja. Sesudah “if” jangan pakai “will”.
id_.whyCorrect: Ini peringatan tentang satu akibat nanti, jadi bagian akibatnya pakai “will” + kata kerja dasar.
id_.whyOthersFail: “Miss” terdengar seperti fakta umum, “missed” bentuk lampau, dan “will missing” menambah -ing sesudah “will”.
id_.howToAvoid: Tanya: ini selalu benar, atau satu kejadian nanti? Lalu pastikan nggak ada “will” sesudah “if”.
id_.memoryCue: Peringatan untuk nanti: “If you…, you will…”

miss.misconception: penanda masa depan hilang dari bagian akibatnya.
miss.whyFails: nggak punya “will”, jadi terdengar seperti fakta umum, bukan peringatan soal bus ini.

missed.misconception: bentuk lampau dipakai untuk akibat yang belum terjadi.
missed.whyFails: bentuk lampau, padahal busnya belum berangkat.

th.objective: ใช้ 'if' + ปัจจุบัน ตามด้วยปัจจุบัน กับสิ่งที่จริงเสมอ และใช้ 'if' + ปัจจุบัน ตามด้วย 'will' + คำกริยา กับผลที่จะเกิดจริงในอนาคต ตัวอย่าง: 'Hurry up! If you don't leave now, you will miss the bus.'
th.misconception: คุณใส่ 'will' หลัง 'if' เพราะเป็นเรื่องในอนาคต หรือใช้รูปอดีตกับความจริงที่เป็นจริงเสมอ
th.reasoning: สังเกต 'Hurry up!' และ 'now' → ดูว่าผลเป็นเหตุการณ์ในอนาคต → รวม 'will' กับคำกริยารูปพื้นฐาน
th.rule: ถ้าจริงเสมอ ใช้ 'If' + ปัจจุบัน แล้วตามด้วยปัจจุบัน ('If you heat ice, it melts') ถ้าเป็นผลในอนาคต ใช้ 'If' + ปัจจุบัน แล้วตามด้วย 'will' + คำกริยา และห้ามใช้ 'will' หลัง 'if'
th.whyCorrect: นี่เป็นคำเตือนถึงผลที่จะเกิดในอนาคต ส่วนผลจึงใช้ 'will' + คำกริยารูปพื้นฐาน
th.whyOthersFail: 'miss' ฟังเหมือนความจริงทั่วไป ส่วน 'missed' เป็นรูปอดีต และ 'will missing' เติม -ing หลัง 'will'
th.howToAvoid: ถามตัวเองว่าจริงเสมอหรือเป็นเหตุการณ์ในอนาคตครั้งเดียว แล้วดูว่าไม่มี 'will' หลัง 'if'
th.memoryCue: คำเตือนเรื่องอนาคตใช้ 'If you…, you will…'

miss.misconception: ส่วนผลไม่มีคำบอกอนาคต
miss.whyFails: ไม่มี 'will' จึงฟังเหมือนความจริงทั่วไป ไม่ใช่คำเตือนเรื่องรถคันนี้

en.objective: Use if + present, present for things that are always true, and if + present, will + verb for one real future result. Example: Plants die if they don't get water.
en.misconception: Learner puts will after if because the event is in the future, or uses the past for a fact that is always true.
en.reasoning: identify the sentence as a science fact -> recall present + present for facts -> choose the present negative for they
en.stem: Plants die if they ___ water.

distractors.misconception: will used after if
distractors.whyFails: It puts won't (will not) in the if part, but that part uses the present.

distractors.misconception: past tense used for a timeless fact
distractors.whyFails: It is past, but this fact is always true.

distractors.misconception: doesn't used with a plural subject
distractors.whyFails: It is for he, she, or it, but they means the plants.

explanation.whyCorrect: This is always true, so both parts use the present, and they takes don't.
explanation.rule: Always true: If + present, present (If you heat ice, it melts). One future result: If + present, will + verb. No will after if.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Won't get' puts will after if, 'didn't get' is past, and 'doesn't get' is for he, she, or it.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is it always true, or one future event? Then check that no will follows if.
explanation.memoryCue: Science facts use the present in both parts.

en.objective: Use a or an when you mention something for the first time, and the when you mention it again. Example: Rina has a cat and a rabbit. The rabbit is white.
en.misconception: Learner uses the for everything or forgets the article, since 'itu' and 'นั้น' can be left out.
en.reasoning: check the first sentence -> notice the rabbit is already mentioned -> choose the article for a known thing
en.stem: Rina has a cat and a rabbit. ___ rabbit is white.

distractors.misconception: indefinite article reused for an already-identified noun
distractors.whyFails: It introduces a new rabbit, but we already know this one.

distractors.misconception: wrong article form regardless of identifiability (vowel-sound rule misapplied)
distractors.whyFails: It is for a vowel sound, and the rabbit is already known anyway.

distractors.misconception: quantifier substituted for a singular countable reference
distractors.whyFails: It is for more than one, but there is one rabbit.

explanation.whyCorrect: The rabbit was mentioned in the first sentence, so now it takes The.
explanation.rule: First mention: a or an (I bought a hat). Second mention: the (The hat is blue), because the listener now knows which one.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' and 'An' introduce something new, and 'Some' is for more than one.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look back: has this thing appeared before? No: a or an. Yes: the.
explanation.memoryCue: Said before? Use the.

id_.objective: Pakai “a” atau “an” saat sesuatu pertama kali disebut, dan “the” saat disebut lagi. Contoh: “Rina has a cat and a rabbit. The rabbit is white.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memakai “the” untuk semuanya atau lupa kata sandang, karena kata “itu” sering boleh dihilangkan.
id_.reasoning: lihat kalimat pertama → perhatikan kelincinya sudah disebut → pilih kata sandang untuk benda yang sudah dikenal
id_.rule: Pertama kali disebut: “a” atau “an” (“I bought a hat”). Disebut lagi: “the” (“The hat is blue”), karena pendengar sudah tahu yang mana.
id_.whyCorrect: Kelincinya sudah disebut di kalimat pertama, jadi sekarang pakai “The”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “A” dan “An” untuk memperkenalkan benda baru, dan “Some” untuk lebih dari satu.
id_.howToAvoid: Lihat kalimat sebelumnya: benda ini sudah muncul? Belum: “a/an”. Sudah: “the”.
id_.memoryCue: Sudah disebut? Pakai “the”.

A.misconception: “a” dipakai lagi untuk kelinci yang sudah disebut.
A.whyFails: memperkenalkan kelinci baru, padahal kelinci ini sudah kita kenal.

An.whyFails: untuk bunyi vokal, dan kelincinya pun sudah dikenal.

Some.misconception: kata jumlah dipakai untuk satu kelinci tertentu.
Some.whyFails: untuk lebih dari satu, padahal kelincinya cuma satu.

th.misconception: คุณใช้ 'the' กับทุกอย่าง หรือลืมใส่คำนำหน้านาม เพราะคำว่า 'นั้น' จะใส่หรือไม่ใส่ก็ได้
th.reasoning: ดูประโยคแรก → สังเกตว่าพูดถึงกระต่ายไปแล้ว → เลือกคำนำหน้านามสำหรับสิ่งที่รู้แล้ว

th.whyCorrect: กระต่ายถูกพูดถึงแล้วในประโยคแรก ตอนนี้จึงใช้ 'The'
th.whyOthersFail: 'a' และ 'an' ใช้แนะนำสิ่งใหม่ ส่วน 'some' ใช้กับมากกว่าหนึ่ง
th.howToAvoid: ย้อนดูประโยคก่อนหน้า ถ้ายังไม่เคยพูดถึงใช้ 'a/an' ถ้าพูดถึงแล้วใช้ 'the'

en.objective: Use a or an when you mention something for the first time, and the when you mention it again. Example: Yesterday I found an old photo in a box. The photo shows my grandma.
en.misconception: Learner uses the for everything or forgets the article, since 'itu' and 'นั้น' can be left out.
en.reasoning: check if the photo is new in the story -> identify the first sound of old -> choose the article for a first mention

distractors.misconception: specific-article overuse
distractors.whyFails: It is for the second mention, which comes in the next sentence.

distractors.misconception: a used before a vowel sound
distractors.whyFails: It needs a consonant sound, but old starts with a vowel sound.

distractors.misconception: negative quantifier used in a positive sentence
distractors.whyFails: It is for questions and negatives, and it does not introduce one new photo.

explanation.whyCorrect: The photo is new in the story, and old starts with a vowel sound, so we say an old photo.
explanation.rule: First mention: a or an (I bought a hat). Second mention: the (The hat is blue), because the listener now knows which one.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'The' comes at the second mention, 'a' needs a consonant sound, and 'any' is for questions and negatives.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look back: has this thing appeared before? No: a or an. Yes: the.
explanation.memoryCue: First time + vowel sound: an old photo. Next time: the photo.

en.objective: Use a or an when you mention something for the first time, and the when you mention it again. Example: We watched a film last night. The ending was very sad.
en.misconception: Learner uses the for everything or forgets the article, since 'itu' and 'นั้น' can be left out.
en.reasoning: check the first sentence -> match the ending to the film -> choose the article for a known thing
en.stem: We watched a film last night. ___ ending was very sad.

distractors.misconception: indefinite article reused for an already-identified noun
distractors.whyFails: It means any ending, but we mean the ending of this film.

distractors.misconception: an used for something the listener can already identify
distractors.whyFails: It fits the vowel sound, but it still means any ending, not this film's.

distractors.misconception: quantifier substituted for a singular countable reference
distractors.whyFails: It is for more than one, but a film has one ending.

explanation.whyCorrect: We know which ending: the ending of the film we just mentioned, so we use The.
explanation.rule: First mention: a or an (I bought a hat). Second mention: the (The hat is blue), because the listener now knows which one.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' and 'An' mean any ending, and 'Some' is for more than one.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look back: has this thing appeared before? No: a or an. Yes: the.
explanation.memoryCue: Part of something already mentioned? Use the: the ending, the actors.

id_.objective: Pakai “a” atau “an” saat sesuatu pertama kali disebut, dan “the” saat disebut lagi. Contoh: “We watched a film last night. The ending was very sad.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memakai “the” untuk semuanya atau lupa kata sandang, karena kata “itu” sering boleh dihilangkan.
id_.reasoning: lihat kalimat pertama → cocokkan akhir cerita dengan filmnya → pilih kata sandang untuk benda yang sudah dikenal
id_.rule: Pertama kali disebut: “a” atau “an” (“I bought a hat”). Disebut lagi: “the” (“The hat is blue”), karena pendengar sudah tahu yang mana.
id_.whyCorrect: Kita tahu akhir cerita yang mana, yaitu akhir film yang baru disebut, jadi pakai “The”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “A” dan “An” artinya akhir cerita yang mana saja, dan “Some” untuk lebih dari satu.
id_.howToAvoid: Lihat kalimat sebelumnya: benda ini sudah muncul? Belum: “a/an”. Sudah: “the”.
id_.memoryCue: Bagian dari benda yang sudah disebut? Pakai “the”: “the ending”, “the actors”.

A.misconception: “a” dipakai untuk akhir film yang sudah jelas yang mana.
A.whyFails: artinya akhir cerita yang mana saja, padahal yang dimaksud akhir film ini.

An.misconception: “an” dipakai untuk benda yang sudah jelas yang mana.
An.whyFails: cocok dengan bunyi vokal, tapi tetap berarti akhir cerita yang mana saja.

Some.misconception: kata jumlah dipakai untuk satu akhir cerita.
Some.whyFails: untuk lebih dari satu, padahal filmnya punya satu akhir cerita.

th.objective: ใช้ 'a' หรือ 'an' ตอนพูดถึงสิ่งหนึ่งครั้งแรก และใช้ 'the' ตอนพูดถึงอีกครั้ง ตัวอย่าง: 'We watched a film last night. The ending was very sad.'
th.misconception: คุณใช้ 'the' กับทุกอย่าง หรือลืมใส่คำนำหน้านาม เพราะคำว่า 'นั้น' จะใส่หรือไม่ใส่ก็ได้
th.reasoning: ดูประโยคแรก → จับคู่ตอนจบกับหนังเรื่องนั้น → เลือกคำนำหน้านามสำหรับสิ่งที่รู้แล้ว
th.rule: พูดถึงครั้งแรกใช้ 'a' หรือ 'an' ('I bought a hat') พูดถึงอีกครั้งใช้ 'the' ('The hat is blue') เพราะผู้ฟังรู้แล้วว่าหมายถึงอันไหน
th.whyCorrect: เรารู้ว่าตอนจบไหน คือตอนจบของหนังที่เพิ่งพูดถึง จึงใช้ 'The'
th.whyOthersFail: 'a' และ 'an' หมายถึงตอนจบไหนก็ได้ ส่วน 'some' ใช้กับมากกว่าหนึ่ง
th.howToAvoid: ย้อนดูประโยคก่อนหน้า ถ้ายังไม่เคยพูดถึงใช้ 'a/an' ถ้าพูดถึงแล้วใช้ 'the'
th.memoryCue: ถ้าเป็นส่วนหนึ่งของสิ่งที่พูดถึงแล้ว ให้ใช้ 'the' เช่น 'the actors'

A.misconception: ใช้ 'a' กับตอนจบของหนังที่รู้แล้วว่าตอนไหน
A.whyFails: หมายถึงตอนจบไหนก็ได้ แต่เราหมายถึงตอนจบของหนังเรื่องนี้

An.misconception: ใช้ 'an' กับสิ่งที่ผู้ฟังรู้แล้วว่าอันไหน
An.whyFails: เข้ากับเสียงสระ แต่ยังหมายถึงตอนจบไหนก็ได้ ไม่ใช่ของหนังเรื่องนี้

Some.misconception: ใช้คำบอกปริมาณกับตอนจบเดียว
Some.whyFails: ใช้กับมากกว่าหนึ่ง แต่หนังมีตอนจบเดียว

en.objective: Use a or an when you mention something for the first time, and the when you mention it again. Example: My mum bought some apples yesterday. The apples were all sweet.
en.misconception: Learner uses the for everything or forgets the article, since 'itu' and 'นั้น' can be left out.
en.reasoning: check the first sentence -> notice the apples are already mentioned -> choose the article for known things
en.stem: My mum bought some apples yesterday. ___ apples were all sweet.

distractors.misconception: some reused for things already mentioned
distractors.whyFails: It means other apples or only part of them, but all shows we mean every apple Mum bought.

distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun
distractors.whyFails: It is for one thing, but apples are many.

distractors.misconception: applies a singular indefinite article to a plural noun and ignores that the noun is already specific
distractors.whyFails: It fits the vowel sound, but it is for one thing and apples are many.

explanation.whyCorrect: The apples were already mentioned, so we use The, also for plural nouns.
explanation.rule: First mention: a or an (I bought a hat). Second mention: the (The hat is blue), because the listener now knows which one.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Some' would mean other apples or only some of them, and 'A' and 'An' are for one new thing.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look back: has this thing appeared before? No: a or an. Yes: the.
explanation.memoryCue: Mentioned before, one or many: the.

Some.misconception: ใช้ 'some' ซ้ำกับสิ่งที่พูดถึงแล้ว

A.misconception: ใช้ 'a' หน้า 'apples' ซึ่งเป็นพหูพจน์
A.whyFails: ใช้กับสิ่งเดียว แต่ 'apples' มีหลายลูก

en.objective: Use a comparative + than for two things and the + superlative for one thing in a group of three or more. Example: Which is bigger, a cat or a dog?
en.misconception: Learner uses the superlative for two things, or forgets the before it, since 'paling' and 'ที่สุด' need no article.
en.reasoning: count the things compared -> identify two animals -> choose the comparative form
en.stem: Which is ___, a cat or a dog?

distractors.misconception: superlative used for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFails: It is for a group of three or more, but only two animals are compared.

distractors.misconception: final consonant not doubled before -er
distractors.whyFails: It forgets to double the g before -er.

distractors.misconception: applies the periphrastic 'more + adjective' pattern to a short one-syllable adjective that takes '-er'
distractors.whyFails: Short words like big take -er, not more.

explanation.whyCorrect: Only two animals are compared, so we use the comparative, bigger.
explanation.rule: Two things: -er or more + than. The winner of a bigger group: the + -est or the most.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'The biggest' is for a group of three or more, 'biger' forgets to double the g, and 'more big' is wrong for a short word.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count what is compared: two things, or a whole group?
explanation.memoryCue: A or B? Use -er: big becomes bigger, fast becomes faster.

id_.objective: Pakai bentuk “lebih” + “than” untuk dua hal, dan “the” + bentuk “paling” untuk satu hal di kelompok tiga atau lebih. Contoh: “Which is bigger, a cat or a dog?”
id_.misconception: Kamu memakai bentuk “paling” untuk dua hal, atau lupa “the” sebelum bentuk “paling”.
id_.reasoning: hitung yang dibandingkan → temukan dua hewan → pilih bentuk “lebih”
id_.rule: Dua hal: -er atau “more” + “than”. Juara dari satu kelompok yang lebih besar: “the” + -est atau “the most”.
id_.whyCorrect: Cuma dua hewan yang dibandingkan, jadi pakai bentuk “lebih”, yaitu “bigger”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “The biggest” untuk kelompok tiga atau lebih, “biger” lupa menggandakan huruf g, dan “more big” salah untuk kata pendek.
id_.howToAvoid: Hitung yang dibandingkan: dua hal, atau satu kelompok?
id_.memoryCue: Pilih A atau B? Pakai -er: “big” jadi “bigger”, “fast” jadi “faster”.

the biggest.whyFails: untuk kelompok tiga atau lebih, padahal yang dibandingkan cuma dua hewan.

biger.misconception: huruf mati terakhir nggak digandakan sebelum -er.

more big.misconception: pola “more” dipakai untuk kata sifat pendek.
more big.whyFails: memakai “more”, padahal kata pendek seperti “big” cukup diberi -er.

th.objective: ใช้รูปขั้นกว่า + 'than' กับสองสิ่ง และใช้ 'the' + ขั้นสูงสุดกับสิ่งเดียวในกลุ่มตั้งแต่สามขึ้นไป ตัวอย่าง: 'Which is bigger, a cat or a dog?'
th.misconception: คุณใช้ขั้นสูงสุดกับสองสิ่ง หรือลืมใส่ 'the' หน้าขั้นสูงสุด
th.reasoning: นับสิ่งที่เปรียบเทียบ → เห็นว่ามีสัตว์สองตัว → เลือกรูปขั้นกว่า
th.rule: สองสิ่งใช้ -er หรือ 'more' + 'than' ส่วนที่หนึ่งของกลุ่มใหญ่ใช้ 'the' + -est หรือ 'the most'
th.whyCorrect: เปรียบเทียบสัตว์แค่สองตัว จึงใช้ขั้นกว่า คือ 'bigger'
th.whyOthersFail: 'the biggest' ใช้กับกลุ่มตั้งแต่สามขึ้นไป ส่วน 'biger' ลืมเพิ่ม g อีกตัว และ 'more big' ผิดสำหรับคำสั้น
th.howToAvoid: นับสิ่งที่เปรียบเทียบว่าเป็นแค่สองสิ่ง หรือทั้งกลุ่ม
th.memoryCue: ถ้าเลือกระหว่างสองอย่าง ให้ใช้ -er เช่น 'fast' กลายเป็น 'faster'

the biggest.misconception: ใช้ขั้นสูงสุดกับสัตว์สองตัว
the biggest.whyFails: ใช้กับกลุ่มตั้งแต่สามขึ้นไป แต่เปรียบเทียบสัตว์แค่สองตัว

biger.misconception: ไม่เพิ่มพยัญชนะตัวท้ายก่อนเติม -er
biger.whyFails: ลืมเพิ่ม g อีกตัวก่อนเติม -er

more big.misconception: ใช้ 'more' กับคำคุณศัพท์สั้น
more big.whyFails: ใช้ 'more' แต่คำสั้นอย่าง 'big' ใช้ -er

en.objective: Use a comparative + than for two things and the + superlative for one thing in a group of three or more. Example: Andi is the smartest student in our class. He always gets 100!
en.misconception: Learner uses the superlative for two things, or forgets the before it, since 'paling' and 'ที่สุด' need no article.
en.reasoning: notice in our class -> identify a group of many students -> choose the superlative with the
en.stem: Andi is ___ student in our class. He always gets 100!

distractors.misconception: comparative used for a ranking within a group of three or more
distractors.whyFails: It compares two people, but Andi is compared with the whole class.

distractors.misconception: the dropped before a superlative
distractors.whyFails: It forgets the; a superlative always needs it.

distractors.misconception: the used with a comparative for a group
distractors.whyFails: It mixes the with a two-thing form; a group needs -est.

explanation.whyCorrect: Andi is compared with the whole class, so we use the + -est, the smartest.
explanation.rule: Two things: -er or more + than. The winner of a bigger group: the + -est or the most.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Smarter' is for two people, 'smartest' needs the, and 'the smarter' mixes the with a two-thing form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count what is compared: two things, or a whole group?
explanation.memoryCue: In our class, in the world: the + -est.

en.stem: My phone is ___ than yours, but Dita's is the cheapest.

distractors.whyFails: It ranks a group, but than compares only two phones.

distractors.misconception: base adjective used without comparative marking
distractors.whyFails: It does not compare, but than needs a comparative.

th.misconception: คุณใช้ขั้นสูงสุดกับสองสิ่ง หรือลืมใส่ 'the' หน้าขั้นสูงสุด
th.reasoning: สังเกต 'than' หลังช่องว่าง → นับว่ามีโทรศัพท์สองเครื่อง → เลือกรูปขั้นกว่า
th.rule: สองสิ่งใช้ -er หรือ 'more' + 'than' ส่วนที่หนึ่งของกลุ่มใหญ่ใช้ 'the' + -est หรือ 'the most'

en.objective: Use a comparative + than for two things and the + superlative for one thing in a group of three or more. Example: This is the most interesting book in the library.
en.misconception: Learner uses the superlative for two things, or forgets the before it, since 'paling' and 'ที่สุด' need no article.
en.reasoning: notice in the library -> identify a big group of books -> choose the superlative for a long word
en.stem: This is ___ book in the library.

distractors.misconception: comparative used for a ranking within a group of three or more
distractors.whyFails: It compares two things, but here the book is compared with the whole library.

distractors.misconception: -est added to a long adjective
distractors.whyFails: Long words take most, not -est.

distractors.misconception: the dropped before a superlative
distractors.whyFails: It forgets the before most.

explanation.whyCorrect: The book is compared with all the books in the library, and interesting is a long word, so: the most interesting.
explanation.rule: Two things: -er or more + than. The winner of a bigger group: the + -est or the most.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'More interesting' is for two things, 'the interestingest' adds -est to a long word, and 'most interesting' forgets the.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count what is compared: two things, or a whole group?
explanation.memoryCue: Long word + group: the most + the word.

en.objective: Use was or were + -ing for a longer action in the past, and the past simple for the short event that interrupts it. Example: We were watching TV when the lights went out.
en.misconception: Learner uses the same form for both actions, since 'sedang' and 'กำลัง' are often left out.
en.reasoning: find the short event the lights went out -> identify watching TV as the long action -> combine were with -ing
en.stem: We ___ TV when the lights went out.

distractors.misconception: treats both clauses as sequential completed events
distractors.whyFails: It makes watching a short finished action, so the idea of being interrupted is lost.

distractors.misconception: singular-past transfer
distractors.whyFails: It is for I, he, she, or it, but the subject is we.

distractors.misconception: present-tense substitution
distractors.whyFails: It is present, but went out shows the story is in the past.

explanation.whyCorrect: Watching TV was the longer action already happening, and we takes were, so: were watching.
explanation.rule: A long action in progress: was or were + -ing. The short event that cuts in: past simple.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Watched' makes it a short finished action, 'was watching' is for I, he, she, or it, and 'are watching' is present.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the two actions: which was already happening, and which happened suddenly?
explanation.memoryCue: Long action: were + -ing. Short event: went out.

id_.objective: Pakai “was/were” + -ing untuk kegiatan panjang di masa lalu, dan past simple untuk kejadian singkat yang memotongnya. Contoh: “We were watching TV when the lights went out.”
id_.misconception: Kamu memakai bentuk yang sama untuk kedua kejadian, karena kata “sedang” sering dihilangkan.
id_.reasoning: cari kejadian singkatnya, yaitu lampu padam → pastikan menonton TV kegiatan yang panjang → gabungkan “were” dengan -ing
id_.rule: Kegiatan panjang yang sedang berlangsung pakai “was/were” + -ing. Kejadian singkat yang memotongnya pakai past simple.

id_.whyOthersFail: “Watched” membuatnya jadi kejadian singkat yang selesai, “was watching” untuk “I”, “he”, “she”, atau “it”, dan “are watching” bentuk sekarang.
id_.howToAvoid: Cari dua kejadiannya: mana yang sedang berlangsung, dan mana yang terjadi tiba-tiba?

watched.whyFails: membuat kegiatan menonton jadi kejadian singkat yang selesai, jadi makna terpotongnya hilang.

are watching.misconception: bentuk sekarang dipakai untuk cerita masa lalu.
are watching.whyFails: bentuk sekarang, padahal “went out” menunjukkan ceritanya di masa lalu.

th.objective: ใช้ 'was/were' + -ing กับการกระทำที่ยาวกว่าในอดีต และใช้ past simple กับเหตุการณ์สั้นที่มาขัดจังหวะ ตัวอย่าง: 'We were watching TV when the lights went out.'
th.misconception: คุณใช้รูปเดียวกันกับทั้งสองเหตุการณ์ เพราะมักละคำว่า 'กำลัง'
th.reasoning: หาเหตุการณ์สั้นซึ่งก็คือไฟดับ → ดูว่าการดูทีวีเป็นการกระทำที่ยาว → รวม 'were' กับ -ing
th.rule: การกระทำที่ยาวและกำลังดำเนินอยู่ใช้ 'was/were' + -ing ส่วนเหตุการณ์สั้นที่มาขัดจังหวะใช้ past simple
th.whyCorrect: การดูทีวีเป็นการกระทำที่ยาวและกำลังเกิดอยู่ และ 'we' ใช้ 'were' จึงเป็น 'were watching'
th.whyOthersFail: 'watched' ทำให้เป็นเหตุการณ์สั้นที่จบแล้ว ส่วน 'was watching' ใช้กับประธานเอกพจน์ และ 'are watching' เป็นรูปปัจจุบัน
th.howToAvoid: หาสองเหตุการณ์ว่าอันไหนกำลังเกิดอยู่ และอันไหนเกิดขึ้นทันที
th.memoryCue: การกระทำที่ยาวใช้ 'were' + -ing ส่วนเหตุการณ์สั้นคือ 'went out'

en.objective: Use was or were + -ing for a longer action in the past, and the past simple for the short event that interrupts it. Example: I was sleeping when my phone suddenly rang.
en.misconception: Learner uses the same form for both actions, since 'sedang' and 'กำลัง' are often left out.
en.reasoning: notice the word suddenly -> identify the ringing as the short event -> choose the past simple form of ring
en.stem: I was sleeping when my phone suddenly ___.

distractors.misconception: aspect confusion (progressive for a single completed trip)
distractors.whyFails: It makes the ringing a long action, but suddenly shows a short one.

distractors.misconception: present-tense substitution
distractors.whyFails: It is present, but was sleeping shows the past.

distractors.misconception: regular -ed added to an irregular verb
distractors.whyFails: Ring is irregular; its past form is not made with -ed.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Suddenly' shows a short event that cut into my sleep, so it takes the past simple, rang.
explanation.rule: A long action in progress: was or were + -ing. The short event that cuts in: past simple.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Was ringing' makes it a long action, 'rings' is present, and 'ringed' is not the past of ring.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the two actions: which was already happening, and which happened suddenly?
explanation.memoryCue: Suddenly = a short event = past simple.

en.misconception: Learner uses the same form for both actions, since 'sedang' and 'กำลัง' are often left out.
en.reasoning: notice the word when -> identify the question as asking about an action in progress -> place were before you
en.stem: What ___ when the teacher came in?

distractors.misconception: singular past be used with you
distractors.whyFails: It is wrong for you, because you always takes were, even for one person.

distractors.misconception: statement order used for a question
distractors.whyFails: It keeps statement order, so it is not a question.

distractors.misconception: present-tense substitution
distractors.whyFails: It is present, but came in shows the past.

explanation.whyCorrect: The question asks about an action in progress when the teacher came in, and you takes were: were you doing.
explanation.rule: A long action in progress: was or were + -ing. The short event that cuts in: past simple.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Was you doing' uses the wrong be for you, 'you were doing' keeps statement order, and 'are you doing' is present.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the two actions: which was already happening, and which happened suddenly?
explanation.memoryCue: In progress in the past? Were you + -ing?

th.objective: ใช้ 'was/were' + -ing กับการกระทำที่ยาวกว่าในอดีต และใช้ past simple กับเหตุการณ์สั้นที่มาขัดจังหวะ ตัวอย่าง: 'What were you doing when the teacher came in?'
th.misconception: คุณใช้รูปเดียวกันกับทั้งสองเหตุการณ์ เพราะมักละคำว่า 'กำลัง'
th.reasoning: สังเกตคำว่า 'when' → ดูว่าถามถึงสิ่งที่กำลังทำอยู่ → วาง 'were' ไว้หน้า 'you'
th.rule: การกระทำที่ยาวและกำลังดำเนินอยู่ใช้ 'was/were' + -ing ส่วนเหตุการณ์สั้นที่มาขัดจังหวะใช้ past simple
th.whyCorrect: คำถามถามถึงสิ่งที่กำลังทำอยู่ตอนครูเข้ามา และ 'you' ใช้ 'were' จึงเป็น 'were you doing'
th.whyOthersFail: 'was you doing' ใช้รูป 'be' ผิดกับ 'you' ส่วน 'you were doing' ใช้ลำดับประโยคบอกเล่า และ 'are you doing' เป็นรูปปัจจุบัน

en.objective: Use was or were + -ing for a longer action in the past, and the past simple for the short event that interrupts it. Example: Rani broke her arm while she was playing basketball.
en.misconception: Learner uses the same form for both actions, since 'sedang' and 'กำลัง' are often left out.
en.reasoning: find the long action was playing -> identify breaking as the short event -> choose the irregular past form of break
en.stem: Rani ___ her arm while she was playing basketball.

distractors.misconception: aspect confusion (progressive for a single completed trip)
distractors.whyFails: It makes the break a long action, but it happened in a moment.

distractors.misconception: regular -ed added to an irregular verb
distractors.whyFails: Break is irregular; its past form is not made with -ed.

distractors.misconception: confuses interrupted past action with present perfect result
distractors.whyFails: It does not go with while she was playing, a finished past time.

explanation.whyCorrect: Breaking an arm is a short event during the longer game, so it takes the past simple, broke.
explanation.rule: A long action in progress: was or were + -ing. The short event that cuts in: past simple.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Was breaking' makes it a long action, 'breaked' is not a real past form, and 'has broken' does not go with a finished past time.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the two actions: which was already happening, and which happened suddenly?
explanation.memoryCue: A short event inside a long one: past simple.

en.objective: Use many and few with countable plural nouns, and much and little with uncountable nouns. Example: There are too many people on this bus. I can't sit down.
en.misconception: Learner uses one word for every noun, since 'banyak' and 'sedikit' work with both kinds of nouns.
en.reasoning: check if people can be counted -> decide if there are a lot or a few -> choose the word for a lot of countable things
en.stem: There are too ___ people on this bus. I can't sit down.

distractors.misconception: applies the uncountable-noun quantifier to a countable plural noun
distractors.whyFails: It is for things you cannot count, but people can be counted.

distractors.misconception: applies the uncountable-noun quantifier ('little') to a countable plural noun, and also confuses scarcity type
distractors.whyFails: It is for things you cannot count, and it means 'not much'.

distractors.misconception: few used when the meaning needs a large number
distractors.whyFails: It fits countable nouns, but it means the bus is almost empty.

explanation.whyCorrect: People can be counted, and the bus is full, so we use many.
explanation.rule: Countable plural (books, friends): many, few. Uncountable (water, money, time): much, little.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Much' and 'little' are for things you cannot count, and 'few' would mean the bus is almost empty.
explanation.howToAvoid: Can you count the noun one by one? Yes: many or few. No: much or little.
explanation.memoryCue: People can be counted: too many people.

th.whyOthersFail: 'little' ใช้กับสิ่งที่นับไม่ได้ ส่วน 'a' ไม่เคยวางหน้า 'many' หรือ 'much'

en.objective: Use many and few with countable plural nouns, and much and little with uncountable nouns. Example: Can I have a little sugar in my tea, please?
en.misconception: Learner uses one word for every noun, since 'banyak' and 'sedikit' work with both kinds of nouns.
en.reasoning: check if sugar can be counted -> notice a before the blank -> choose the word for a small amount
en.stem: Can I have a ___ sugar in my tea, please?

distractors.misconception: few or a few used with an uncountable noun
distractors.whyFails: It is for countable plural nouns, but sugar cannot be counted.

distractors.misconception: a placed before many
distractors.whyFails: It cannot follow a, and it is for countable nouns.

distractors.misconception: of dropped after a lot
distractors.whyFails: It needs of after it, and it means much, not a small amount.

explanation.whyCorrect: Sugar cannot be counted, so a small amount is a little.
explanation.rule: Countable plural (books, friends): many, few. Uncountable (water, money, time): much, little.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A few' is for countable nouns, 'a many' is not English, and 'a lot' needs of.
explanation.howToAvoid: Can you count the noun one by one? Yes: many or few. No: much or little.
explanation.memoryCue: A little sugar, a little milk, a little time.

id_.objective: Pakai “many” dan “few” untuk benda jamak yang bisa dihitung, serta “much” dan “little” untuk benda yang nggak bisa dihitung. Contoh: “Can I have a little sugar in my tea, please?”
id_.misconception: Kamu memakai satu kata untuk semua benda, karena “banyak” dan “sedikit” bisa dipakai untuk benda apa saja.
id_.reasoning: cek “sugar” bisa dihitung atau nggak → perhatikan “a” sebelum titik-titik → pilih kata untuk jumlah yang sedikit
id_.rule: Benda jamak yang bisa dihitung (“books”, “friends”): “many”, “few”. Benda yang nggak bisa dihitung (“water”, “money”, “time”): “much”, “little”.
id_.whyCorrect: “Sugar” nggak bisa dihitung, jadi jumlah yang sedikit pakai “a little”.
id_.whyOthersFail: “A few” untuk benda yang bisa dihitung, “a many” bukan bahasa Inggris, dan “a lot” butuh “of”.
id_.howToAvoid: Bendanya bisa dihitung satu per satu? Bisa: “many/few”. Nggak bisa: “much/little”.
id_.memoryCue: “A little sugar”, “a little milk”, “a little time”.

many.whyFails: nggak bisa didahului “a”, dan untuk benda yang bisa dihitung.

lot.whyFails: butuh “of” sesudahnya, dan artinya pun banyak, bukan sedikit.

en.objective: Choose at for a point or a place for an activity, in for inside an area, and on for a surface or a floor. Example: My uncle lives in Surabaya.
en.misconception: Learner uses one preposition for every place, since 'di' and 'ที่' cover them all.
en.reasoning: identify Surabaya as a city -> recall the word for inside a big area -> apply it before Surabaya
en.stem: My uncle lives ___ Surabaya.

distractors.misconception: at used for a city or country
distractors.whyFails: It is for a point, like a bus stop, not for a whole city.

distractors.misconception: on used for a city or country
distractors.whyFails: It is for a surface, but a city is an area we live in.

distractors.misconception: movement preposition used for a static location
distractors.whyFails: It shows movement, but living somewhere is not moving.

explanation.whyCorrect: A city is a big area, so we use in.
explanation.rule: At: a point or a place for an activity (at the bus stop, at home). In: inside an area (in Jakarta). On: a surface or a floor (on the second floor).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'At' is for a point, 'on' is for a surface, and 'to' shows movement.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: a point, an area, or a surface or floor?
explanation.memoryCue: Cities and countries: in Surabaya, in Thailand.
